svg.title: TREDECIM architecture
svg.desc: An event starts a durable episode. Recall, decide and act are checkpointed to CockroachDB. Before money moves the decision is re-validated under FOR UPDATE, and the memory revision (closing one interval, opening the next on the facts table) commits in the same serializable transaction as the ledger insert and the balance update. A partial vector index over WHERE valid_to IS NULL serves semantic recall. Amazon Bedrock Titan Embed v2 supplies embeddings only and is not in the decision loop.
svg.text: BITEMPORAL MEMORY FOR AI AGENTS · ALLEN, 1983
An event starts an episode. Every step is checkpointed. The memory revision and the money move commit in one transaction.
02 EPISODE · DURABLE STATE, NOTHING IN PROCESS MEMORY
served by the partial vector index
Embeddings only. Not in the decision
The episode keeps nothing in the process.
Each transition is written to episodes
before the next begins. Kill the worker:
resumes from the checkpoint; the decision may be old
SELECT … FROM facts WHERE valid_to IS NULL FOR UPDATE
Re-validate against live memory before any money moves.
Destination changed, version bumped, or a freeze: abort, nothing written, back to recall.
closes the open interval; the row survives

present, not the size of the history.
Eight agents race; one row lands.

belief and money land together, or neither does.
The recovery sweep reads this index and
Replay is safe: side effects are idempotent
or transactional, so nothing pays twice.
The aborts are the interesting rows.
Seven refusals in the eight-agent race
are the system working, not failing.
p50 commit latency is read from here,
written after the transaction resolves: commit, abort, or retry
A vector store ranks by similarity alone and has nowhere to put valid_to IS NULL. Here validity and
distance are evaluated by one engine, in one transaction: semantic recall cannot return a closed fact.
npm run verify asserts these claims against a live cluster: the
invariant, the query plan, the refusals, and the mid-flight resume.
